goal_objective: Advance fix/refresh-queue-throughput: Raise the production refresh queue's throughput so the self-sustaining whole-market universe (34k active instruments, ~76k queued jobs on 2026-11-20) can be prepared and kept fresh: cheap claims, more concurrent drains, and no duplicate children per maintenance pass.. Acceptance criteria: AC1: An additive Alembic revision and the model declare a partial index for claimable jobs (priority, next_attempt_at, id where status is queued, retry, deferred or leased). On real PostgreSQL the production claim query uses it with many completed rows present, and the revision reverses cleanly.; AC2: The drain chain cap defaults to 6 and the worker's job slots come from a setting (default 10). The effective chain cap always leaves slots for the scheduled jobs. The quarter-hour tick tops live drains up to the cap only when due work exists.; AC3: A later-hour ensure of the same identity tuple reuses the open queued, deferred or retry identity child and records both parents. A completed negative child keeps the hourly recovery behaviour, and a leased child is not reused.; AC4: A later maintenance pass for the same instrument, timeframe, adjustment and deepest range reuses the open history child, extends its end to the later end (open-ended counts as latest) and records both parents. Explicit-start ranges, derived-only children and leased children are not merged, and a sibling with a later end is reused unchanged.; AC5: Exact-source feature CI and the staging exhaustive gate are green before promotion; production deployment waits for the human's approval.. Required local profile: docker_integration. Stop at ready_for_human_review; do not integrate, promote, deploy, or modify another worktree.
